markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **protected-recent prefix dropout** within corrected BERT4Rec, after repairing diagnostic category identity. No improvement is established: the supplied curriculum scored 0.5375 versus baseline 0.5425.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Separately normalized branches make objective weights explicit. Their coefficients must remain identical between experimental arms. (2) A scheduling result needs an exposure-matched constant control. Current scores do not establish scheduling benefits. (3) Serving parity stopped before scoring because ModelView.dataset_name was invalid. Consequently, stale-history dependence remains unmeasured.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec already includes terminal supervision [1]. Novelty must concern context corruption rather than appended-mask prediction. (2) Recency Sampling motivates better alignment between training targets and next-item prediction [2]. It does not establish that deleting older context helps this benchmark. (3) Q-BERT4Rec explores structured masking alongside other changes [3]. Its results cannot isolate corruption-policy benefits here.

**Framework.** Three directions separate mechanisms: objective allocation changes which losses dominate; context selection changes available evidence; representation enrichment changes item information. Hold objective allocation and representations fixed while testing context selection.

Candidate assessments below use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each entry gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matched-mean constant terminal weight [1] | 2: attributable; established | 5: useful control; narrow | 5: inference alignment; indirect | 5: tests separation; pooled margins | 2: scalar change; paired sampling |
| Protected-recent prefix dropout [2,3] | 4: targeted corruption; familiar regularization | 7: cheap context study; context loss | 7: targets stale/broad cues; purpose unobserved | 6: tests margin robustness; no sensitivity evidence | 3: training-only change; position safeguards |
| Joint title residual encoder | 4: compliant combination; familiar content fusion | 6: sparse-item sharing; extra cost | 6: specific wording; lexical shortcuts | 4: richer features; no content diagnostic | 6: one network; vocabulary/export work |

**Selected idea.** On terminal examples only, independently replace 15% of visible positions preceding the final two history items with attention-masked PAD holes. Preserve absolute positions, recent items, target identity, and final MASK. Keep interior examples and the existing coefficient schedule unchanged; compare against that exact schedule without dropout.

This targets two reported user failures: outdated interests competing with current behavior, and broad historical associations outranking specific recent matches. Both links are hypotheses; recent events need not reveal current intent. The model-facing target is sampled-pair ranking errors, currently approximately 4.0–5.7%, with Electronics showing the lowest tenth-percentile margin, 0.683.

First repair category identity and verify checkpoint/export parity. Then compare frozen terminal diagnostic margins and available history interventions, alongside unchanged host macro validation HR@10. Train one model per category per arm; never combine arms. Preserve seeds, routing, limits, sampling and negative proposals. Dropout requires no inference change, additional predictor, unavailable attributes, or target timestamps.

idea.description: Protected-recent prefix dropout: regularize the terminal-prefix branch of corrected BERT4Rec by removing a small fraction of older visible context while preserving its two most recent items. Train exactly one independent model per category and serve exactly one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies outdated interests and broad associations displacing specific current matches. Selectively corrupting older context may reduce dependence on such cues while preserving recent evidence, although neither purpose nor recency dependence has been quantitatively established. The model-facing hypothesis is improved sampled positive–negative separation, particularly the weaker Electronics margin tail. Supplied diagnostics measure in-sample errors, not validation improvements; parity and sensitivity remain unavailable because category identity is invalid. The prior curriculum's supplied validation score is below baseline, so this proposal makes no improvement claim.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected architecture and canonical predictor writer unchanged. Apply dropout only to the terminal branch after its leakage-free prefix construction and before model.log2feats. For each row, identify real visible history positions, protect the final two, and independently drop each remaining position with probability 0.15. Set dropped IDs to PAD=0; do not compact, backfill, reindex surviving positions, or remove the terminal MASK. Short prefixes with at most two visible items remain unchanged. Ensure attention actually excludes PAD holes and valid-query outputs remain finite. Hide targets and their suffix before corruption; earlier repeated target IDs are legitimate observed context. Keep all interior targets, target counts, loss reductions, negative proposals, optimizer settings and objective coefficients identical to the control.

For the initial comparison retain the supplied curriculum exactly: alpha(e)=0.5+0.3*min(e/100,1), using zero-based epochs and the same configured epoch count in both arms. This comparison estimates corruption under that curriculum; it does not establish a scheduling advantage. Do not add a simultaneous recency sampler, content encoder, hard-negative objective or new coefficient. Use dedicated RNG streams so augmentation does not advance sampling, initialization or model-dropout RNG differently. Pair users, endpoints, interior masks and negatives across arms where the host permits.

Before interpreting diagnostics, set ModelView.dataset_name to the actual routed category rather than a generic family label. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual trained view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and public-data interfaces. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Record training-prefix provenance directly during construction; tensor checks alone cannot establish it. Preserve unmodified frozen diagnostic panels separately from training augmentation. Compare terminal and interior margins separately rather than treating their pooled baseline as a terminal-only estimate.

Verify exact checkpoint state identity and finite float32 logits across actual module, ModelView and exported working/predict.py. Cover short, full-length, truncated and mixed-length histories, singleton/batch agreement, and PAD holes; use atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4. For left padding, appended MASK readout is the final position; general nonpadding readout uses the greatest valid index, never count-1. History sensitivity remains unavailable until the existing full parity gate passes. No residual-patching result or embedding collapse is established by supplied measurements.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Use a single GPU and trial-local artifacts. All controls, parity checks and diagnostics count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Use identical checkpoint opportunities and the fixed host macro validation HR@10 for selection. Run the no-dropout control and proposed augmentation only if both fit the remaining budget; do not attribute cross-run historical score differences solely to augmentation. Export one selected checkpoint per category from the chosen trial, without score fusion, checkpoint averaging or checkpoint reuse from other trials.

Only histories, titles, descriptions and historical timestamps are available; this experiment uses histories alone. Do not infer ownership, compatibility, satisfied needs or simulator traits. It does not directly solve duplicate-supply recommendations, and dropping older context can erase enduring preferences. User-alignment assessment: 7/10, positive—explicitly targets stale interests and broad association shortcuts; negative—recent context is only a proxy for specific purpose. Model-alignment assessment: 6/10, positive—provides a controlled test of sampled-ranking robustness; negative—history dependence is unmeasured and training margins need not predict host HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch


def protected_recent_dropout(sequence, mask_id, augmentation_generator, p=0.15):
    """Terminal rows only; sequence is B x L, left padded, on CPU.
    augmentation_generator is a dedicated torch.Generator seeded with 42.
    Call before moving the batch to GPU. Preserve absolute positions.
    """
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or sequence.shape[1] < 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected B x L terminal sequences')
    if sequence.device.type != 'cpu':
        raise ValueError('Use the dedicated CPU augmentation stream')
    if not torch.all(sequence[:, -1].eq(mask_id)):
        raise ValueError('Terminal rows must end in reserved MASK')
    visible = sequence.ne(0) & sequence.ne(mask_id)
    if not torch.all(visible.any(dim=1)):
        raise ValueError('Every terminal example needs visible history')
    # Reverse cumulative count identifies the two latest real history positions.
    from_right = visible.flip(1).long().cumsum(1).flip(1)
    eligible = visible & from_right.gt(2)
    draws = torch.rand(sequence.shape, generator=augmentation_generator)
    dropped = eligible & draws.lt(p)
    augmented = sequence.clone()
    augmented[dropped] = 0
    return augmented, dropped

originality.positive: Protecting the most recent evidence while corrupting older terminal context gives an explicit, testable context-selection hypothesis within corrected BERT4Rec.
originality.negative: Context dropout and structured masking are established; this is a modest policy refinement rather than a new model family or learning principle.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost controlled comparison could establish whether context robustness merits later work on learned context selection.
future_potential.negative: Older interactions may encode enduring preferences, and sampled validation gains would not establish better full-catalog usefulness or the proposed behavioral mechanism.

code_difficulty.positive: The algorithm changes training inputs only and adds no parameters, inference computation or independent predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Internal PAD handling, preserved absolute positions, paired RNG streams and the existing diagnostic parity defect require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Includes terminal-item masking and appended-mask inference, establishing the family-correct foundation and terminal-supervision control.
limitations: Terminal supervision itself is established and cannot substantiate novelty for this proposal.
Does not establish that protected-recent prefix dropout improves the supplied four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Next-Item Recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary motivates aligning training-target selection with next-item recommendation.
Provides motivation for studying the task relevance of historical evidence.
limitations: Target recency sampling and selective context dropout change different distributions.
Does not prove that this BERT4Rec model relies excessively on stale interests.

related_work.title: Q-BERT4Rec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes exploration of span, tail and multi-region masking.
Motivates treating corruption structure as an experimental axis.
limitations: Also introduces multimodal semantic representations and quantization, preventing attribution of overall results to masking alone.
Provides no matched evidence for the proposed history-only dropout policy under the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
